title: Privacy Policy
subtitle: How PG Cashflow handles, protects, and stores personal data under the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023.
dpdpCommencementNotice: Certain provisions and Rule 4 commenced on 13 November 2026, with substantive provisions and remaining Rules scheduled for commencement on 13 May 2027.

sections.heading: 1. Data Fiduciary & Overview
paragraphs: This Privacy Notice outlines how PG Cashflow operates as a Data Fiduciary under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (“DPDP Act”). Certain provisions and Rule 4 commenced on 13 November 2026, with substantive provisions and remaining Rules scheduled for commencement on 13 May 2027. We are committed to data minimization, purpose limitation, and absolute transparency regarding personal data collected from property owners, managers, and tenants.

sections.heading: 2. Data We Collect & Purpose
paragraphs: We collect only the minimum data strictly necessary to facilitate verified tenancy, dues accounting, and security operations:
bullets: Contact Identifiers: Mobile phone number (used for one-time password authentication and essential transactional push notifications).

Identity Proof (Aadhaar / Government ID): Processed via Smart OCR document upload or offline UIDAI Secure QR through certified verification gateways. We collect full name, date of birth, and masked UID (only the last 4 digits, e.g., XXXX-XXXX-1234).

Payment & Ledger Records: Payment transaction references, payment mode (UPI, card, netbanking), due identifiers, payment status, and settlement timestamps. Bank account details for refund/payout settlement are processed directly through certified payment aggregators.
Tenancy & Operational Metadata: Building, room, and bed allocation, move-in and exit dates, meal RSVPs, and maintenance logs.

sections.heading: 3. Explicit Prohibition on Unmasked Aadhaar Storage
paragraphs: In strict compliance with the Aadhaar Act, 2016 and UIDAI regulations:
bullets: We never store raw, unmasked 12-digit Aadhaar numbers or biometric data.
Aadhaar verification is entirely voluntary; tenants are entitled to provide approved alternative identification (PAN, Voter ID, Driving Licence, or Passport).

Where identity documents or attested photos are submitted for verification, source bytes are encrypted at rest using AES-256-GCM while pending review and are purged from primary verification storage upon manual owner approval or verified consent revocation. Only minimal verification metadata (such as masked UID, keyed deduplication hash, status, and audit timestamps) is retained during active tenancy and applicable statutory periods.

sections.heading: 4. Data Security, Encryption & Storage
paragraphs: All data in transit is encrypted using Transport Layer Security (TLS 1.3). Sensitive identity and transaction records at rest are secured using AES-256 encryption. Access to tenant records is restricted by role-based scopes (Wardens cannot view owner bank accounts or tenant financial histories outside their building). Documents are served exclusively through authenticated, role- and property-scoped API endpoints with strict no-store caching directives and access audit logging.

sections.heading: 5. Data Retention & Erasure
paragraphs: Financial and ledger records are retained for active tenancy plus statutory limitation periods mandated by applicable tax and accounting laws in India (e.g., maintaining financial books for up to 7 years). Raw identity document bytes submitted for KYC are purged upon manual approval or consent revocation, while minimal verification metadata and audit records are retained only as required for active tenancy, deduplication, and compliance.

sections.heading: 6. Rights of the Data Principal
paragraphs: In alignment with the DPDP framework, you have the right to:
bullets: Access a summary of personal data held about you and processing activities undertaken.
Request correction or completion of inaccurate personal data.
Withdraw consent for optional communications and request data erasure upon tenancy termination.
Nominate an individual to exercise rights on your behalf in the event of incapacity.

sections.heading: 7. Grievance Officer & Inquiries
paragraphs: If you have questions, feedback, or grievances regarding your data, contact our designated Grievance Officer:
